assumptions.summary: icing-practice premise: no refrigeration -> gut immediately -> ice -> drain meltwater. Transfer boundary: Separate handling practice from a five-day freshness duration.
uniform-price premise: one Scottish market context -> location variation negligible -> fixed price. Transfer boundary: Retain time, port, grade, species, inflation, and demand limitations.
surface-stock premise: near-surface harvest -> depth temperature ignored -> SST proxy. Transfer boundary: Daily vertical migration does not establish that depth is inconsequential.
small-trawler premise: under-12m vessel -> at most 4 knots -> midwater trawling. Transfer boundary: Check consistency with 51 km radius, five-day freshness, and daily trips.
instant-detection premise: sonar/acoustics -> locate schools quickly -> search time ignored. Transfer boundary: Detection capability does not eliminate transit, search error, weather, or catch time.

constant-population premise: high fecundity + quotas -> births offset deaths/catch -> fixed schools. Transfer boundary: Fecundity alone does not establish recruitment, survival, stock, or quota equilibrium.
zero-capture-time premise: pelagic trawl while moving -> capture simultaneous -> travel-only clock. Transfer boundary: Retain tow, haul, sorting, unloading, and turnaround time.

trend-continuation premise: current climate practices -> decades to change -> similar 50-year SST rate. Transfer boundary: Use climate scenarios and structural uncertainty rather than a single extrapolation.

seasonality-cancellation premise: annual SST oscillation + natural fish migration -> long-run cancellation -> trend-only field. Transfer boundary: Seasonal behavior must be modeled or validated before claiming cancellation.
seven-day mortality premise: intolerable patch -> seven days -> school death. Transfer boundary: Specify consecutive versus cumulative exposure and reset logic.
density-independence premise: 27.75 km cell -> enough nutrients -> no crowding. Transfer boundary: Correct the cell length/area and support carrying capacity.

temperature-only migration premise: temperature fatality -> dominant rule -> predation/pollution omitted. Transfer boundary: Name the omitted drivers and prevent a one-driver run from becoming a most-likely claim.

contributions.summary: Uses one slope and intercept per grid coordinate rather than a single global warming rate.
Combines ICES density levels for 70% of schools with an explicit 30% unobserved-population component.
Connects continuous thermal-distance descent intuition to a daily local-search implementation.
Separates optimal, staying, and tolerable temperatures for herring and mackerel.
Runs fish movement and ten-vessel capacity-limited revenue inside one daily simulation.
Evaluates disappearance time and gross revenue at 87 possible Scottish coastline points.
Reruns the complete fit and ABM under lower and upper NOAA measurement-error histories.
Tests relocation, target-species substitution, and refrigeration within related spatial interfaces.
Stops quantitative claims at territorial-water and EEZ quota implications the model does not estimate.
Turns the technical chain into a dated two-column fishery newsletter with four direct actions.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: spatiotemporal data intake: 1982-2019 daily OISST -> Scotland crop -> 0.25 deg grid -> 64x80 array. Transfer boundary: Publish exact product version, latitude extent, missing values, and retrieval date.
per-cell fitting loop: 13,879 days -> x day index -> SST y -> slope A/intercept B -> 5,120 cells. Transfer boundary: Mask land and missing data over all dates, not only the first slice.
parameter-field disclosure: cell fits -> A map + B map -> daily forecast function. Transfer boundary: Use correct N50-N66 extent and retain slope units.
landings-to-fish proxy: 2018 tonnage -> grams/fish -> accessible individuals -> assumed school size. Transfer boundary: Landings are removals, not total harvestable abundance; keep the proxy label.

ICES-to-agent initialization: 2003-2006 rectangle means -> six density levels -> 70% weighted sprouts -> 30% random. Transfer boundary: Report scaling, coordinate transform, seed, and excluded rectangles.
fleet-statistics normalization: 1,079 t/1,539 vessels -> fish mass -> 1,750 mackerel or 2,800 herring. Transfer boundary: Annual landed tonnage per vessel is not necessarily physical trip capacity.

net-weight-to-stochastic range: filled net/net mass -> target fish weight -> vessel capacity -> 5.7% -> 3%-7%. Transfer boundary: Reconcile 45-5 versus printed 45-40 and species-specific denominators.

landed-value normalization: annual species value -> currency conversion -> tonnage/fish mass -> dollars/fish. Transfer boundary: Publish the herring result and use the correct exchange-rate direction and date.

measurement-error scenario construction: NOAA err -> +/-1.96 err per observation -> best/worst arrays -> refit coordinate models. Transfer boundary: A coherent pointwise measurement bound is not a forecast scenario or trend confidence interval.
coefficient-table disclosure: latitude 50 row -> longitude -15 to 3.5 -> A/B/land entries. Transfer boundary: A sample cannot reproduce the full 64x80 coefficient field.

87-site result disclosure: coordinate -> three-run mean accessible days -> mean revenue -> species tables. Transfer boundary: Retain censoring, precision, replicate variation, and coordinate-domain conflicts.

download-to-array pipeline: daily URLs -> NetCDF sst/err -> roll longitude -> crop 64x80 -> pickle -> regress. Transfer boundary: Clipped lines, product paths, environment versions, and full error handling are required for reproduction.

independent_extensions.summary: multi-driver extension: predators + food + nutrients + temperature -> habitat suitability -> migration. Transfer boundary: Require data, causal mechanism, calibration, and ablation.

parameter provenance extension: freshness/radius/capacity sources -> common vessel archetype -> uncertainty propagation. Transfer boundary: Use matched definitions and units rather than averaging incompatibilities.
trend-to-seasonal extension: daily SST climatology + seasonal fish behavior -> short-term paths -> long-run average. Transfer boundary: Validate both seasonal phase and climate trend.
three-run-to-ensemble extension: seed ensemble -> mean/quantiles -> port ranking stability -> tail risk. Transfer boundary: Predefine convergence and decision-stability criteria.
quota-scenario extension: stock shares -> EEZ agreements -> Scottish quota -> company catch cap -> net revenue. Transfer boundary: Use dated law and explicit access scenarios.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Seven short Summary blocks make the forecast-agent-company-strategy chain rapidly scannable while preserving headline quantities.
A domain-authentic two-column article demonstrates audience adaptation through a map, four numbered actions, and a dated imperative close.
Five explicit questions and section pointers make deliverable coverage auditable in the absence of a separate official task file.
Spatial A/B fields communicate why one regional average is insufficient, provided extent and uncertainty are reconciled.
Matched six-snapshot panels make the herring/mackerel thermal-response contrast easy to compare.
The four-panel 87-site map links ecological access and money in one judge-readable decision artifact.
Explaining the counterintuitive mackerel scenario through route entry shows useful mechanism-aware interpretation, conditional on censoring and seed checks.
Explicitly calling quota effects a possible revenue overestimate is stronger than pretending the legal system was quantified.

models.summary: Forecast daily SST independently at every ocean grid coordinate. Map day since Jan. 1, 1982 through coordinate-specific slope A and intercept B.
Estimate simulated herring agents from landed tonnage and fish mass. Convert 38,138 metric tonnes to 1.525e8 fish and divide by assumed school size.
Estimate simulated mackerel agents from landed tonnage and fish mass. Convert 75,022 tonnes and 400 g/fish to 1.875e8 fish and state 4,000 schools.
Measure a patch's deviation from species optimum. Take the absolute difference between local SST and optimal temperature.
Derive the local direction of increasing thermal distance. Take partial derivatives of thermal distance with respect to grid coordinates.
Relate negative thermal gradients to fish coordinate velocity. Set dx/dt and dy/dt equal to negative coordinate partial derivatives.
Package the time-dependent fish coordinates. Write the school path as a planar vector with zero third coordinate.
Update school locations on a daily dynamic temperature field. Stay below threshold, move toward the patch closest to optimum, or escape randomly from a local minimum.
Remove schools after configured intolerable-temperature exposure. Increment a death counter above tolerance and kill after the threshold.
Estimate fish capacity per small vessel. Divide annual small-vessel landings by vessel count and average fish mass.
Estimate fraction of vessel capacity caught per attempt. Convert stated net fish weight to fish count and divide by species vessel capacity.
Convert species landed value and tonnage to dollars per fish. Apply an exchange rate and divide annual value by fish count.
Simulate ten daily vessel trips from one fishing port. Visit every school within radius, apply random catch, cap at vessel capacity, and accumulate price times fish.
Measure how long any school remains within a port radius. Update last-catch with the current tick while at least one school is in range and cap at 2070.
Construct lower and upper SST histories and refit cell regressions. Subtract or add 1.96 times NOAA error before rerunning the complete model.
Compare monthly herring revenue at four cardinal-direction sites. Run the same ABM at Shetland, Aberdeenshire, Dumfries, and Hebrides and mention relocation cost.
Apply the movement/access/revenue interface to haddock. Use an unreported parameter bundle to produce haddock access and revenue maps.
Estimate revenue with on-board refrigeration. Triple the 51 km radius from a five-to-fifteen-day freshness ratio and rerun four ports.
Represent how stock movement may change Scottish quota influence. Map stock shares among EEZs to a possible Scottish quota and company revenue cap without claiming a fitted rule.
Align the 1982 SST origin, 2006 ABM start, and 2070 stop. Add start-offset to ticks and stop at a hard-coded target day.

named-location contrast: east Iceland little change -> east England +2 C -> heterogeneous slopes. Transfer boundary: Quantify locations and uncertainty rather than rely only on color.

snapshot route result: NE Scotland/Shetland -> Iceland cool tongue -> sparse Scottish clusters -> east Iceland. Transfer boundary: Report distribution, replicate variation, and territorial/EEZ status.
snapshot route result: west Ireland/Scotland arc -> northward wave -> Scotland/Faroe line -> southern remnants. Transfer boundary: Reconcile panel references and code's 25 C mortality rule.
species-wide time result: 87-site mean 16,584 days -> about 2051/2052 -> northern maxima. Transfer boundary: It is a mean of censored last-access values, not one company deadline.
site ranking result: Shetland $44m -> Aberdeenshire $36.3m -> Orkney $26m -> minimum $2,540. Transfer boundary: Reconcile Summary $42m, appendix coordinates, and gross/net terminology.
species-wide time result: 21,168 days -> about 2064 -> many censored at 2070 -> eight-plus-year gap. Transfer boundary: Censoring makes ordinary averages and year differences biased.

site ranking result: Shetland $204m -> Highlands $163m -> Outer Hebrides $65m -> Firth of Forth under $30k. Transfer boundary: Retain species price, capacity, port coordinate, and 64-year simulation horizon.

monotone temperature response: upper 11,974 -> baseline 16,584 -> lower 18,328 days -> near five-year lower gain. Transfer boundary: Do not use a qualitative 'significant' claim without stochastic uncertainty or test.

nonmonotone finite-horizon response: lower 20,612 -> baseline 21,168 -> upper 21,454 -> southeast schools move into range. Transfer boundary: Separate route-entry benefit from long-run warming harm and use matched seeds.
northern relocation result: $89k/month plateau >30 years -> later decrease -> four-port ordering. Transfer boundary: Compare total discounted net value after relocation cost.

spatial decision result: north consistently higher -> millions more -> $400k cost -> recommend Shetland. Transfer boundary: The paper mentions cost but does not subtract it in the shown revenue curves.

alternative-species time result: longest/most consistent disappearance -> broad Scottish viability -> north retains mackerel advantage. Transfer boundary: Publish the actual parameters and site table.
alternative-species value result: south-to-north stock -> continued fishing -> demersal gear drawback. Transfer boundary: Revenue is not profit and bottom-trawl transition costs are omitted.

four-port percent result: Shetland +42.9 -> east +124 -> west +735.8 -> south +1700.8 percent. Transfer boundary: Absolute revenue, cost, distance, and capacity saturation matter alongside percentage gain.
heterogeneous-benefit explanation: dense north already fills capacity -> radius adds little -> sparse south gains schools. Transfer boundary: Verify daily full-capacity frequency and stock depletion.

12-nm nonconflict conclusion: fish north -> Denmark/Iceland territorial belts -> far from Scottish relocation -> no border issue. Transfer boundary: Fishing routes, not only port sites, may cross zones; retain caveats.

management-risk conclusion: stock shifts -> Iceland/Greenland share -> Scottish influence falls -> revenue may be overestimated. Transfer boundary: Keep this qualitative unless quota scenarios are modeled.

limitations: No separate official 2020 Problem A statement was found; task reconstruction uses the paper's five-question restatement.
source_quality.notes: Five contact sheets, nine detail sheets, and direct original formula/code pages were inspected. Several code lines are physically clipped and initialization arrays are explicitly truncated. MATHmodels footer/QR text was excluded; no AI Use Report is present.
source_quality.text_fidelity: All 39 physical-page text segments were read sequentially and visually reconciled against rendered pages.

task_reconstruction.decision: Choose location, target species, or vessel capability while treating quota effects as a qualitative boundary.
task_reconstruction.objective: Forecast 50-year herring and mackerel locations, quantify access and gross-revenue effects for small Scottish fishing companies, and evaluate adaptation under jurisdiction constraints.

unresolved_questions.summary: No separate official 2020 Problem A statement is present in the corpus; task reconstruction relies on the paper's five questions.
Is the intended region N50-N60 as defined, or N50-N66 as required by the 64-row code, figures, and port tables?
Where are the claimed residual plots, seasonal autocorrelation tests, spatial checks, and holdout errors?
Why are annual Scottish landings treated as total accessible population, and what uncertainty follows?
What school size converts 1.875e8 mackerel to 4,000 agents when Figure 7 says 20,000 fish per school?
What physical speed and latitude/longitude metric turn the thermal gradient into dx/dt and dy/dt?
What complete parameter bundle and code path produced herring rather than the printed mackerel defaults?
How does annual landed tonnage per vessel map to physical capacity per trip?
Was net fish weight intended as 45-5=40 kg, and how was one 5.7% value applied to both species?
What is the printed herring price and which dated euro-dollar exchange direction produces $0.50 mackerel?
Does daily harvest reduce fish available in a school, or can the same school yield new catch indefinitely?
What seed, variance, confidence interval, or convergence evidence supports averaging only three runs?
How are ports that never see fish coded in last-catch averages versus ports that lose access immediately?
Why do pointwise 95% measurement-error bounds represent climate best and worst futures?
Which real port, workforce, capacity, cost, and transition constraints define a feasible relocation?
Where are haddock temperature, depth, abundance, price, catch, vessel, and code parameters?
How do 4 knots and five or fifteen days yield 51 km and 153 km operating radii?
Which stock-sharing agreement, EEZ share, quota rule, and Scottish license scenario limits company catch?
Why is Jan. 1, 2006 represented by 25*365 days after Jan. 1, 1982, and how are leap days handled?
Where are the clipped NetLogo expressions, truncated arrays, complete species configurations, full Python URLs, files, versions, and seeds?

verification.summary: fit-diagnostic check: linear fits -> residual inspection -> no high-level structure -> accept line. Transfer boundary: Publish residual plots and quantify seasonal autocorrelation and spatial dependence.
field-level plausibility check: independent A/B cells -> coefficient maps -> named spatial contrast. Transfer boundary: Independent fits may create spatial discontinuities; validate field smoothness.
2020-vs-2070 visual check: same field/color form -> warmer palette -> 1.59 C mean. Transfer boundary: Use a common color scale and report land/mask treatment.

stochastic averaging check: per port/species -> three simulations -> average time/revenue -> map. Transfer boundary: Three runs are insufficient to characterize tail risk without variance or convergence.
input-bound propagation check: two altered SST cubes -> full refit -> full ABM -> outcome maps. Transfer boundary: Match seeds and include parameter/model uncertainty.
geographic transfer check: north/east/south/west ports -> same model -> monthly curves -> spatial ranking. Transfer boundary: Four exemplars do not validate all 87 or real relocation sites.

capability counterfactual check: same herring/ports -> 1x vs 3x radius -> revenue differences. Transfer boundary: Hold all inputs matched and account for cost before calling the counterfactual beneficial.

weaknesses.summary: The Summary calls the forecast and revenue horizon 50 years, but the ABM starts in 2006 and the tables extend to 2070, a 64-year interval.
The article says southern and western coasts lose herring within 20 years, while the baseline mean points to about 2051 and only the upper case is near 2038.

The Summary and article cite roughly $42 million herring revenue, while the baseline body and Appendix A2 report a Shetland maximum around $44 million; Table 3 uses $42.18 million for a selected north site.
The Summary/body present three solutions, while the public article presents four by splitting transition to mackerel from harvesting haddock.
The Summary reports refrigeration gains from about 43% to over 1700%, while the article says 50% to over 1700%.
The Scotland Region is defined as N50-N60, but a 64-row 0.25-degree grid, Figure 3, Python extent, and Appendix sites use N50-N66 or reach N63.75.
A 0.25-degree cell is described as having area about 27.75 km2, but 27.75 km is approximately the north-south side length; area is much larger and longitude width varies with latitude.
Strong annual oscillation is visible in Figure 2, yet the paper says residuals have no high-level structure without displaying residual diagnostics and then omits seasonality.
Independent cell regressions have no holdout test, uncertainty band, spatial regularization, or climate-forcing scenario for extrapolation to 2070.
Scottish landings are treated as total accessible herring abundance even though removals are not a stock census.
1.525e8 herring divided by 20,000 per school is about 7,625 schools, rounded to 8,000 without an uncertainty rationale.
1.875e8 mackerel divided by the Figure 7 value of 20,000 per school is about 9,375 schools, not the 4,000 agents used in prose and code.
Equating path velocity directly to the negative thermal-distance gradient omits a movement-rate coefficient, coordinate metric, units, and boundary conditions.
Equation 6 merely states R(t)=<x(t),y(t),0> after saying the component equations are integrated; no solution, initial condition, or numerical integration is supplied.
The prose calls the discrete neighbor logic equivalent to the continuous gradient equations without quantifying discretization, scaling, or tie behavior.
A one-third-patch move often leaves a turtle on its previous patch, so the subsequent prev-patch equality can trigger escape mode even after a valid directed step.
Escape mode is described as lasting at most 10 days, while code sets random 30, producing values from 0 through 29 days.
The death counter never resets when temperature returns below tolerance, so exposure is cumulative rather than seven consecutive days.
Code kills only when death-counter > death-time, so with death-time 7 a school dies after the eighth counted hot day.
Printed setup-fish values are mackerel defaults only; the paper does not show a complete, reproducible herring parameter switch.
Equation 7 uses annual landed tonnage per vessel as if it were physical per-trip vessel capacity.
The prose first states 1,070 tonnes but Equation 7 uses 1,079 tonnes.
Equation 8 prints 45 kg - 40 kg even though the text says a 45 kg filled net and 5 kg net; the claimed 5.7% requires 40 kg of fish, or 45-5.
One 5.7% catch proportion cannot arise identically for both species when fish mass and vessel fish capacity differ unless the weight-level formulation is shown consistently.
The displayed currency conversion and annual value/tonnage inputs do not transparently reproduce the rounded $0.50 mackerel price, and no herring price result is printed.
The company loop treats each turtle as a school but the visible code has no school fish-count state or catch depletion, permitting repeated daily revenue from persistent agents.
The PDF physically clips the core trip-revenue and capacity expressions, so the printed harvest calculation cannot be executed or fully audited.
last-catch is updated whenever any turtle is in radius, not when a positive capacity-feasible catch is actually made.
Only three stochastic runs per one of 87 sites are averaged, with no seeds, variance, intervals, or convergence criterion.
Disappearance times are right-censored at 2070 but averaged as ordinary values; many mackerel sites equal the cutoff.
start-offset=25*365 does not represent Jan. 1, 2006 from Jan. 1, 1982; the exact interval is 24 years plus leap days.
The until-2070 target 32141-start-offset conflicts with table maxima of 23,375 days and omits an explicit exact-date convention.
Adding or subtracting 1.96 times measurement error to every historical observation does not by itself define a 95% confidence interval for future climate trend or a best/worst scenario.
Herring upper/lower differences are called significant without stochastic intervals or a statistical test.
Ports that never receive a fish may retain last-catch=0, mixing never-accessed sites with immediate disappearance and contributing to the reversed mackerel mean.
The herring baseline 16,584 days after Jan. 1, 2006 is around mid-2051, yet body text says around 2052 and the conclusion says 2056.
Relocation uses four fixed illustrative ports and gross revenue curves rather than optimizing a feasible relocation path or deducting the cited $400,000 cost.
Haddock output maps are shown without the temperature, depth, population, price, catch, mortality, or code parameters needed to reproduce them.
At 4 knots, five days of continuous travel is far greater than 51 km; the independent 51 km source radius is simply tripled for refrigeration without a closed speed/time/range calculation.
Table 3 calls values rounded to the nearest $100,000 but prints values such as $8,895,798 and inconsistent lower-order precision.
Revenue is repeatedly called profit or benefit although relocation, refrigeration, fuel, labor, permits, gear, maintenance, quota, discounting, and risk are omitted.
The article says Iceland and Greenland have free reign to reduce Scotland's quota, while the body only supports a conditional shift in management influence and possible overestimate.
The territorial-water analysis checks distance from proposed ports but not whether vessel routes to migrating fish cross foreign territorial seas or require EEZ access.
The strengths section calls the stochastic sample size large even though reported decisions use only three repeats per site.
The strengths section gives coordinate examples N20,S20 and N20,S30, which are not valid latitude-longitude pairs for Scotland.
The conclusion gives a 2070 regional range of 8-12 C while the reported regional mean is 12.05 C, which cannot exceed the stated maximum range.
The conclusion recommends haddock as a profit-restoring strategy despite absent net-cost and gear-transition calculations.
NetLogo arrays are explicitly truncated for presentation and multiple statements/comments run beyond the PDF right edge.
Python download URLs and several NetCDF/plot expressions are physically clipped, so the acquisition and fitting script is incomplete.
The printed Python code creates lower and upper SST arrays but the shown T_regs fitting block loads and fits only the baseline file; scenario refitting requires undocumented manual changes.
The forecast plot maps 31,879 evenly spaced samples to 1982-2070 while evaluating only 13,879+18,000 days, short of the actual calendar interval.
